answer: Nothing (EUR 0). The question's premise is false: the ECB made no profit in 2025. It recorded a loss of EUR 1,254 million (2024: loss of EUR 7,944 million), and the Governing Council decided to carry this loss forward on the ECB's balance sheet, to be offset against future profits. So there was no 2025 profit distribution to the Banque de France or to any other NCB. The Banque de France's capital key is 16.3575%, with subscribed and paid-up capital of EUR 1,771 million.

evidence.text: The ECB’s loss for 2025 was €1,254 million, compared with a loss of €7,944 million in 2024. Following a decision by the Governing Council, this loss will be carried forward on the ECB’s balance sheet and offset against future profits.
Like the previous two years, the Governing Council decided to carry the loss forward on the ECB’s balance sheet to be offset against future profits.

notes: False premise: there is no 2025 ECB profit to distribute. The capital key of 16.3575% is confirmed (subscribed capital EUR 10,825 million in total). The accounts show no interim profit distribution for 2025. Applying 16.3575% to a loss would be meaningless, because losses are not passed on to NCBs as negative distributions; they are carried forward.

answer: Belfius' consolidated cost of risk was EUR 80 million (net provision) in 2025, against EUR 133 million in 2024. That is EUR 53 million lower, about -40% (the press release says 'fell by 40%'). The 2025 net provision consists of EUR 186.6 million of provisions for non-performing (phase 3) loans (2024: EUR 249.3 million), partly offset by a net reversal of EUR 106.3 million on substandard (phase 1 and 2) loans. 186.6 - 106.3 = EUR 80.3 million, which rounds to the reported EUR 80 million.

evidence.text: the total cost of credit risk fell by 40% to €80 million (net provision)

Provisions for non-performing loans (phase 3) amounted to €186.6 million (compared with €249.3 million in 2024), to which was added a net reversal of €106.3 million on substandard loans (phases 1 and 2).

notes: The 80.3 vs 80 difference is rounding. The change is -53m / 133m = -39.8%. Cost of risk is shown as a negative P&L figure (-133 / -80); p.10 labels it 'Impairments on financial instruments and provisions for credit commitments'. Figures are unaudited. The 2024 phase 1/2 component is not given; the implied value is 133 - 249.3 = a net reversal of about 116.3.
